This book left me nothing but a heavy and confused heart!!! Gah! This is love to the next level! Now I realized that one can be selfish when it comes to love. One can be greedy when it comes to love. And one is willing to risk it all when it comes to love! 
 Olivia is one hell of a confused girl. She shoves Caleb away from her then one day she's doing everything to win him back and then mess things up and break up with him then win him back again then mess things up again... It's a pathetic and strenuous cycle! I guess the reason why she's too guarded it's because of what happened to her family. He's father has always cheated on her mother that she even witnessed the cheating unfold in front of her. The kind of love she has grown with is not the kind of love that anyone of us is experiencing. She's confused as to what love is. 
 Caleb, you're one hell of a romantic guy! But I hate you because you're one hell of a womanizer! How dare you? I fell in love with you! But how could you? You could've fought even harder for the girl you want... You just let things slip in the way. 
 I really can't fathom my feelings with this book. I love how I get accustomed to different emotions when I read this book. I just felt like reading this book was like taking a roller coaster ride, there were a lot of highs and lows in this book. Its a good thing because it leaves you curious and it leaves you wanting more. 
 I wish this has a sequel! Gah!!! 
 Wanna take a roller coaster ride? Read this book!

I was in a bookstore searching, inquiring, going through all the stalls for Colleen Hoover's books but the battle search just lead me into this book. I knew right away when I saw this book that I've marked it as my "to read" book. With the money intended to buy Colleen Hoover's books but since there aren't available yet, I gambled on this book. It's quite expensive from its neighboring paperbacks but I know there was something special about this book that made me want to buy it. I actually held it for awhile because I might come across with lesser valued book with a great story but I just saw myself standing in front of the cashier, grabbing a grand, the bar code scanned, handing the money to the girl, have the amount typed, handing me my change, get's the receipt, putting the book inside the brown paper bag with red print and grabbing the item and shoving it inside my bag. So in short, I bought it... 
 Anyway, ever since I read Anna and the French Kiss I got so in love with Paris! That I started buying a planner with the Eiffel Tower emblazoned on it, sticky notes with anything Paris, pens and a lot more!!! I got so excited when I knew that one of the settings of the book is in Paris... but not like other books which's story often happens in the Eiffel Tower, Lourve, Notre Dame... the book touched on places I've never heard but got my interest into it. It showed a different facet of Paris. A facet that only a true Parisian can tell but was successfully put into words and descriptively liven up by the writer. 
 The book was more on self-discovery and having a say in Life. Allyson, unfortunately, had her life plotted chronologically by her parents. She was the kind of daughter who every parents want to have. Obedient, understanding, respectful, studious, submissive, adventure averse person, good girl... Until after she arrived from her European tour that everything that she was once known started making her ask herself if that's the kind of girl she still wants to be or if she wants to be the person she has made herself up when she was in Paris.... Care free, independent, happy, always thirsty for adventure! 
 I'd like to elaborate more on this book but I'd be giving out spoilers. Anyway, I love how this book was different from those that I have read. I love how she has found herself during her journey and how far she came to find the answers to her year long questions and she has transformed herself to becoming the person she always want to be.

The story was too heavy for me. I pushed myself to finish reading this book because it'll leave me with a heavy heart. The things that happened to Echo's life was way too HEAVY and I couldn't imagine what my life would be if I had hers. Same goes to Noah. Their lives were full of misery but when they found each other, they turned their miseries into happiness. It's just nice to know that in this chaotic world, you'll always find someone who shares the same misery as yours, same happiness as yours and shares the same passion and love as yours. I like that every chapter Echo and Noah got to speak. I just got annoyed with the friends of Noah. But hey! It was a good book but too heavy though.

My hopes were high with this book. Judging from the plot, the reviews, the ratings. I thought I already found a book better than Slammed and Point of Retreat. But I was disappointed :( 
 The shift of the story was too abrupt and I can't identify whether it's still part of the previous scene or is it a new one... There were a lot of problems that weren't resolved in the story like what happened between Nan and Sam? Are they gonna still be friends? Have the Garret's forgiven Sam's mother? What happened to Tim? Was he able to successfully get out of his parents lives and have a fresh start? The story just simply ended without resolutions to the problem. 
 The story has already built its momentum when the accident happened. But eventually, the momentum disappeared and all was left was doubts and questions in your mind... Arghh!! 
 The scumbag man, I forgot his name! The campaign adviser of Sam's mom! He's a dick! I hate him, he's very unforgiving and inhumane! How can such person exist? 
 Somehow, there were also interesting parts in the story. Like when Jase and Sam finally met after how many years of thinking the other doesn't exist. When they finally kissed! When they did it... The awkward part when they both bought the tampon and couldn't decide which to choose because they were both innocent in such thing. When Jase kept on thinking what happened the other night, when they did it, he was completely distracted he hammered his thumb and Sam kissed it and Jase kept on saying he had an injury in some other parts which Sam all kissed. Gah! 
 I also love Will, the walking encyclopedia of the family, he never runs out of trivia! He's such a great child!! I never knew that when you drop a coin from the Empire State Building someone will die! Such a wiz! 
 Anyway, the book wasn't like what I expected it to be... However, it was good.

The start of the book was quite slow and I didn't grasped what it was trying to imply to its readers. I didn't liked her fashion sense, referring to Lola and her dirty punk rock boyfriend, Max. The book only got interesting on the part where Cricket started appearing. 
 This book established Perkins identity to her readers. She's fond of writing stories on unrequited love. 
 I like how she inserted Anna and Etienne on the story. I like how their relationship progresses. Etienne is now thinking of their future which is kinda cute because knowing that they are still young but they already foresee the future of being together. 
 Over-all, it was average. Not the same impact it created on me on the first book.

I love-hate this book! I love this book because it shows that, a lot of things can happen and these things happen in the least you expect it. It's a different treatment on teenage love stories. Before I mention everything I love, I'd like to talk about what are the things I hate about the book. It would've been nicer if it was a first person treatment. The main caharcter could've told the story so that the emotions were more humane, more personal and more intimate. 
 There were parts when she told the story about herself, the narration was too much that it gets boring. If the author treated it in a personal context, people would've cared for her and understood where her emotions come from. 
 I love the kissing part! I love how Oliver was just so real and he really just can't contain his feelings that he just bursted into kissing Hadley. I love how they can just talk about topics people normally talk about when they reached years of being together. They're only random people but they talk as if its forever. 
 Over-all, this book is an interesting book to read.

For giggle and romantic part, I'd like to rate it 3 because it's so lame to know that Roger and Amy have to fell in love towards the end of the story. But, however, I love how Amy has to pour in all of the pain that was welling up on her to Roger so that she can gauge if Roger is really someone for keeps. When Roger accepted and in fact pointed out to Amy that she wasn't cause of her father's death, that was when Amy let her walls come down and just felt the urge of becoming reckless and kissed Roger as if her life depends on it. 
 For the treatment of scenes, I like how Morgan Matson put flashbacks every end of a chapter so that the readers will know how the events from the previous chapter occured and how was it triggered. 
 For the use of words, I'd say it was good but somehow I felt like Morgan was afraid to use difficult words because her book's target audience are the teenagers. It's important for you to know the language that your target audiences speak so that you'll know how to make use of your vocabulary and you'll know what to write and what you ought not to write. 
 For the uniqueness, I'd rate it 4.5 because of naming the chapter as CHAPTER 1, etc. The author put quotes that'll explain what the chapter is all about. Well, not necessarily explain but somehow would put to sense what the whole chapter tries to imply. 
 For the lessons I've learned, I'd rate it 5. There's just to much to learn from the book. It felt like it was a multi-faceted book. 
 "The best discoveries always happened to the people who weren't looking for it." 
 "It's not about the destination. It's getting there that's the good part. 
 "We can't know what's going to happen. We can just try to figure it out as we go along.

I love how simple the story was told but the meaning of each words leave you think and make you realize. Auggie was indeed the epitome of courage, strength and wisdom. I love how each of the key characters had a chapter to show their own perspective. And each of them lead to one thing, their love and concern for Auggie. I really broke down on the graduation part. It was really a heart breaking scene and I can picture out how people who use to insult him, who use to talk behind his back and who use to scare away from him as if he has a contagious disease.

I love Gossip Girl series. I've been hooked since high school. My sense of fashion has been greatly influenced by Serena and confidence by Blair. Although there were quite changes when it was on series. I already expected it to be as such but nevertheless, I still liked it. Although it was too short, it seems like I was just given a glimpse of all the worst that might happen on the following books.

We should see with our hearts not with our eyes. This is the lesson I've learned from reading The Little Prince. I was convinced to read this book because my favorite professor, Sir Elson, told me that this was his favorite book. I've been hearing about this book and I was expecting it to be thick and in hard bound. But to my surprise, it was just thin. You can finish reading it in a couple of hours. I love that there were illustrations! It teaches a lot of lessons. Such an awe-inspiring book.

... If I woke up in a different body every day-if you never knew what I was going to like tomorrow-would you still love me? 
 That line in the book tore my heart apart. Simple for us to utter words but it's hard to do it. And it even gets harder when you're actually in the situation wherein you have to choose from being with the only person you've loved so much but you have to carry the burden of seeing him in different bodies everyday or get away from that person but you're heart is shattered into pieces every time you're not with him. 
 There's so many things to love about this book. ...I love the anticipation it gives me, I'm excited to know what body A inhabits this time. I love how A save the lives of the helpless people he inhabits and how he completely make things memorable before he leaves the body he inhabits. I love how he makes an effort to see Rhiannon every time he gets a chance, I love the effort that Rhi has to put through just to see A. I love the strength and courage that Rhi showed, it's definitely hard... Really it is. You have kept a lot of things from people because you know they wont believe you otherwise, the pain of not being able to introduce A to her friends because she knows the next day he'll be a different person, the pain of not being able to stay the night with him and wake up the next morning with him because there are so many risks, the pain of not being able to introduce him to your parents and the pain of loving someone but he's different, physically, every day. 
 One of the most painful parts of the book was when A attended the funeral of the grand father he inhabited. Clearly, he's not directly related to this person but all of the sudden he just cries during the eulogy not because he felt for the death of the grand father but because he realized, he'll never experience the things that the old man is experiencing. When A dies, no one will speak good things about him, no one will tell them about the craziest and most memorable experiences they had, no one will feel like there's someone missing in their lives and no one will cry for him when he dies. 
 I love the part when he inhabited the body of Alexander. My favorite body conquest. He told Rhi that they'll meet in the bookstore and pretend like it's the first time they met so that these are the memories he's going to leave to Alexander. He chose Alexander to take care of Rhi because he knows that Rhi and Alex shares the same passion and he knows that Alexander will give the same amount of love that A has given to Rhi. They started counting the remaining minutes until midnight, Rhi kept kissing A. Gosh! If only I can put my emotions here and share to you how much pain I felt and tears that fell when I read this part. Indescribable.

I.LOVE.THIS.BOOK. I was only starting to read the book but I immediately got hooked. It's like I don't want to stop from reading it because I felt hanging. I was in a train ride when I was reading this, I grinned like an idiot and if I was the only person in the train, I would've started screaming and giggling. There's too many great scenes. There were also scenes I got too emotional. I don't want to stop reading this book but there's also a part of me who wants to stagger reading this book. The most painful part for me, as a reader, is that when you have established a bubble for you and the book it felt like there's only two things... You and the book... and when you are almost finished, you have a fear that "that" bubble you have established will just pop out. 
 I love how Stephanie Perkins connected with her readers. Her choice of words were impeccable, the lines were simple yet striking, her jokes were funny and everything was real and you can feel the emotions of the characters. 
 I also love that she introduced Parisian culture, breath-taking landmarks and a lot if information I only knew when I read the book. It makes you want to go to Paris as soon as possible! 
 I love how she also mentioned a lot of movies. Haven't heard any of those from the book but I think I'll check them out. 
 Anna and Etienne are among my favorite book couples. Their relationship has definitely evolved. Unlike in other books, they skip some parts that's why you get confused, "Hey are they now together?", "How exactly they become an item?".... And as their friendship evolved, their feelings has also evolved.... It deepened.... Until it became complicated but they got through it. 
 I'm just really sad that I finished reading this book. It has a sequel but a different story. It's frustrating!!! I want to know what comes next.... 
 I urge everyone to read this book!!! It's perfect!

This ain't a book with to die for characters, impeccably romantic scenes, heart warming dialogues and non-pseudonym authors. This book doesn't have a continuity in story nor does have parallelism in structure. This book doesn't consist of lengthy chapters and heart pumping, beguiling love scenes. This book is not your ordinary book. This book was written for you. And was written for me as well. 
 There's just too many great lines to choose from that somehow pokes your senses and makes you realize the truth behind what's hidden underneath. This book, upon seeing the cover will awaken your interest and make you grab it. The name of the author itself is intriguing that you want to really find out what's written in his masterpiece. The titles were short yet sums up the content. The pictures were creepy yet were artistically taken. 
 Different. Captivating. Truthful.

I was quite disappointed with the book. It was as if I was reading Fifty Shades Trilogy. The three books were compressed in this book. Although according to some reviews, the sexual scenes here were really realistic unlike Fifty Shades (I don't know the extent of it's being realistic because haven't experienced it). But it was a good story though with a somehow different perspective.
I loved it! It's a story anyone can relate to.

I've read this book out of curiosity. I've been seeing this book on the racks of Fully Booked next to Fifty Shades Trilogy. So I was thinking this is another erotic novel. But because reading erotic novels have woken my curiosity, I bought the book. I was expecting something more because it's what romance give out to their readers right? But it doesn't mean I haven't seen more, I don't like it anymore. I loved it... I loved how the author kept it light, how he first talked about the pleasure of waiting, how he emphasized the importance of being cared for, being loved, being respected... Because this were the things that Julian never experienced. Things that were deprived of her, things that were only shown to her by Gabriel. I loved the book because it mentioned a lot of classic songs, classic novels and foreign languages. I loved how the author emphasized the importance of waiting for the right person before giving up one's virtue because honestly, in today's generation, people no longer cares if he/she's the right person for as long as they satisfy their humanly needs. The lines were very novel-ish. I hoped the author made it a little conversational, something realistic because there were some lines which were unrealistic to me that one couldn't afford to utter. Over-all, I love the book and I'll definitely buy the next one.

Among the Alice Series, this is my favorite!!! The book has discussed a lot of important issues and one of which is "giving away your virtue". I know in other countries being virgin is really an issue for them. Luckily, Alice didn't gave away her virtue to someone so undeserving. It's a good thing that Alice and Patrick are back together! I love them so much! Alice deserves someone like Patrick who is ambitious and knows what he wants in life. Among the scenes they had, my most favorite was when Patrick went to Alice's house to help in arranging things after their house was remodeled. They just sat down and Alice sat on Patrick's lap and they were just gazing on the fire. And Alice said "It's good to have you back" and Patrick said "Good to be back"... Aww!!!
This books reminds me of Molly McAdams's Taking Chances. The book has a lot of highs and lows which makes the story interesting and captivating.

It took me quite sometime to finish reading this book. I had high hopes for this books because of the high rating it received but however, it ended up disappointing me. The story was different from among the books I've read but it didn't immediately grabbed my attention. There wasn't much of a heart pumping part, there wasn't much of giggle, there wasn't much of explosion of emotions. 
 Anyway, I really do adore Lucas. The story, on the other hand, gave a new breath to what we usually perceived of bad looking guys. Yes he has tattoos, yes he has several piercings, yes he drives the motorcyle, yes he wears fitted clothes, yes he has long hair but not too long, yes he;s into fights, yes a lot of girls are eyeing on him, yes to all bad looking guys you imagine but what makes him different is that he is a badass smart guy and he makes himself useful. He's not wallowing around like other bad looking guys I've read. 
 What I realized about this book is that you can't love completely a person without confronting and dealing with each others demons . I know each one of us has gone through a lot of hell in life, an experience which we don't and never would want to revisit. But time will come, no matter how much we try to hide it, it'll eventually get out like a steam. Next thing you'll know your past and present are instantly colliding that you don't know how to deal with it anymore. That's what happened to the characters of the story. What made them go through the storm was that they trust each other and their love was undoubtedly greater than their demons, greater than anything else in this world that's why they end up together.

This is my favorite Nicholas Sparks novel. The story is indeed a page turner. You can feel different emotions while reading this book. I love how Nicholas write books because he doesn't stick to what is already known to us. He tries to put a different angle to stories.
This book was only interesting because of its illustrations but the story was such a blur. It doesn't have any continuity and you'll end up being puzzled on why they really broke up.
BEYOND WORDS!
Fair enough.
What can I say... Modern woman in 18th century. I love this book! My husband and I loved the show and had to read the books! Highly recommend!

** spoiler alert ** 
 At first I thought Darcy's character reminded me of a modern Scarlett O Hara. The way she acted and really the way she transitions is like Scarlett O Hara in the Scarlett book. Growing as a woman and mother. I really liked and I knew I had to finish the book tonight

Oh Kitty Wright. What can I say about this character... she has a lot of sides to her... and I think I liked this book more than the first. I had to keep reading... harder to put the book down. Anyways once again closeness to detail.. at points felt like I was reading a semi different version to Gone With the Wind and Scarlett mixed. Good book... can't wait to read book 3 of the Saga.

I am a history buff and can be very critical of those who right historical romances. What I liked about Love and War was the authors careful consideration to history and facts. I have done research on some of the battles that she listed in the book... and this being a free book from Amazon was a great way to introduce me to the author. You are swept up in the constant troubles of Kitty Wright... who was the southern belle who wasn't like all the other girls... and the fact that she has love triangles, drama, and action... I enjoyed the book very much... so much so that I bought 2 and 3 to continue on with their story.
I thought at parts it was a wee bit I don't know Cheesy... but the sex scenes definitely kinda got ya in the mood...lol. And I liked the lead guy Chris. He was funny and sweet. :)

Okay So I will admit this book had its points where it made me think about '50 Shades of Grey'. I liked it... but at points I wondered if maybe it went to far. Don't get me wrong I really liked the book but the similarities to Grey was crazy. Its always with Billionaires...lol. Anyways still interesting sex scenes, story lines, and characters. It will be interesting to see how the next book pans out.

OMG. Okay the title specifies that this is for guys... so I couldn't help but wonder what the author wrote for guys about the book. Okay so I read all three books. I loved them. Now when I jokingly asked my boyfriend to read them (And no I would not make Adam read '50 Shades') I wanted to see what this had to say. With the book that has spawned so many commentaries and sparked so many sex lives it was not surprising to find out that guys might not be interested thus creating this book. I liked this book. The Chapters are summarized by the author to be a guide to help guys spice up the sex life... and how he writes about the book is funny. He mentions using your quivering lips often, make sure to accentuate them when you are with a woman, and carry around Kleenex's and marker you initials on them to represent Grey following Ana's drunken Stupor. I giggled and I'm sure people outside of the store wondered where the loud laughs were coming from. :D

Never in my life did I think I would feel horrible for an alien inhabiting a human. I loved the book...at times I wondered how it was going to end and at parts it was slow...but I would read more like it... Cant wait for the movie!

Okay so book 3 in the SAGA. Well I liked it... but at points I still feel a bit of whats the word... maturity in the writing. I try to say this in a way that does not defer the book. It reminds me so much of Twilight... but I also find it very different. I will say one thing I went from one book to the next. I remained involved. I can't wait to see how 4 turns out.

This book was twisty. I almost need to write my comments at the end of the 4th book. The main character Nora Grey is at it again with her boyfriend Patch who happens to be a fallen Angel... or at least he was until he saved her life--- was given back his wings and made her Guardian Angel. They are trying to date but the Archangels don't like that...so she has to decide if she stays with him despite the fact that he will go to hell if he stays with her... or she breaks up... and attempts to move on... is it really that easy???

This was a free book I actually grabbed because a friend's picture was on the Cover as the hero... Brad. Anyways I liked the book. I felt that at times I had problems really connecting with what was going on... although I was able to pick up very fast what was going on when (SPOILER) she loses her virginity after being married for 7 years to the lead guy. And then the guy was trying to get her pregnant. I got that pretty fast... but I will admit at first I thought he was trying to get her pregnant to bring up some scandal to get them into society.

Not bad... A pretty quick read... my only qualms were that the beginning started off rocky... she did okay... but I felt at parts it was a little cheesy. Also I feel that if '50 Shades' and 'Marriage of Convenience' had a baby this would be it.

Safe Haven. What can I say. There is romance. Danger. I actually felt the book very closely reminded me of a friend and what she would want done. Almost as if she was speaking to me now as she passed away a few years back. The book has twists and I read it in a few hours. I could not put it down. I loved it and recommend it to everyone! Now to find which Nicholas Sparks I will read next :)

I liked the story line. I kept wondering how Jane Feather was going to pull it off, I mean you have a main character Clarissa who is claiming she is a whore... when really she is of noble blood. She constantly kept the lead character in the loop... gosh she was good at making up lies... but good story... can't wait to read #2... which I found out I already had prior to buying this book lol. :D
Although a good book... I was a little lost in the beginning. Took me a while to get into it. It does have some interesting twists... that I was not expecting.

Okay so book 2. I loved it. (SPOILER) Felt like they did a good job picking up where 1 left off. We are back to Beatrice aka Tris post battle simulation and she must try to figure out a way to take down ERUDITE... Also finding out who else is Divergent. Another good book!

Okay I read this at the recommendation of my cousin and I will say that I loved it. It was only 2 books but I loved how involved it was. I read the Hunger Games within a matter of hours--- being it was a pretty fast read, and found Divergent to be the same. It is the beginnings of this futuristic society that takes place in Chicago area. There are 5 factions and at the age of 16 the teenagers are tested based on their aptitude. From what I could pull to summarize - Abnegation is Selflessness - meaning these people go out of their way to help people, Dauntless - Brave--- more of your Thrill seeker, Amity - Peaceful people--- always calm, Erudite- Intelligence creates the technologies that the rest of the area uses, and Candor - Truth--- Truth is valued above all. The original reason for creating these factions was that war was the result of selfishness (Abnegation), cowardliness (Dauntless), dishonesty (Candor), Greed (Amity), and pretty much lack of education (Erudite). The lead character Beatrice Prior is 16 and she must decide what she is on her aptitude day when she is actually channeled into 3 possible factions which is unheard of. People with this are known as DIVERGENT and are thought to be dangerous being that they can not technically be controlled. 
 I felt this book had Danger, and romance, I mean I kept involved the entire time... and the author defiantly didn't waste time in between books. Good book!

What I liked best about this book is it answered a lot of questions that I had about the Twilight Saga. The Histories were awesome, especially showing the genealogy of the Quilette lines. I would find it awesome if she continued on with this series... she has so many possibilities that she can go with and I'm sure there are a lot of fans who feel the same. My points that I think she could go into would be - Renesmee and Jacob Romance, Of course the Volturi are gonna be pissed that they got shown up, Also Nahuel's dad now technically has another Hybrid to test his theory... so I'm imagining some kind of a fight for the heart of Renesmee... or trying to kidnap her... Can Jacob and Renesmee have children? Also there is the Children of the Moon-- They said they were all but extinct... meaning there could still be some out there...so an introduction of werewolves... maybe trying to fight Volturi or the Cullens... who knows... I just don't think it is right to end the series like this... Also I read Midnight sun--- I Believe that Meyer should continue with this idea - I liked reading Edward's thoughts as well as seeing what people were saying in their thoughts about Bella. I would have Midnight Sun - finished, New Moon - have Jacob's thoughts in a book and Edwards thoughts, Eclipse - have Jacob and Edward's thoughts, and Breaking Dawn have Edward's Thoughts. And if she were to create a series about Renesmee and Jacob to still use the Cullens because they are part of Renesemee life. The fact of the matter is the Cullens --- are not only talented... but now their coven went from 8 people to 9... and now you have the wolves -- and their coven friends... the fact is they are a force to be reconned with...which means as long as there are Vampires - there are wolves... meaning not only does Jacob live forever as long as he stays near Renesmee... but the Cullen's coven is getting larger because of Renesmee. She is their link. So many possibilities... I hope Meyer takes them. I realize she likes to get into other books... but she left herself wide open with this! :D

I wish it were finished... but from what I could read this would have been or will be an awesome book. I like looking at Edward's perspective. I didn't know if I would before. I hope she continues forward with this and follows through with the other books. I mean it gives an interesting perspective. I also said that she should make Renesme and Jacob's saga. I love the series! :D

I found this book interesting. I wondered how Riley was able to control his newborn army knowing what problems Jasper faced previous. It was a short book but I thought it was an interesting look into a newborn vampire.

Breaking Dawn. What more can I say? Action, romance, drama... I mean this book has it in spades. It is a long book... but I could not put it down. I teared up a few times. I wish there was more. I was imagining Robert Pattinson and Kristen Stewart fighting the battle against the Volturi, and I was concerned for them in general. Loved the series... she needs to continue! WOW!.

When I read this I giggled a lot. I mean I loved Jacob and Edward's banter. They both are still fighting for Bella's love but in the end she needs to decide what she wants. I also love the history. The movie makes reference to the histories but this book goes so much more in depth which I love. I feel like I can see the characters clearer.

I liked the second book. I mean. It once again explained things a little bit better... but I don't know... it seemed like the film might have been better in this case because it condensed it yes... but it was an okay condense.
Not bad--- felt that as a History buff there were some questionable uses of medical terminology and wording. But still a good book! Very twisty!

I like this author. She got my attention early on and kept me going the whole time. My only concern which goes for a lot of authors in Historical Romance is that use of Language. By this I mean sometimes they are so into the writing that they might miss when they make references or at least use words that of of this time.
(SPOILER) Connected to the main characters... happy it didn't end with another pregnancy as so many romance novels do now a days. But she was using darker settings.

HILARIOUS!!! :D I love the original Hunger Games --- but won't deny this made me giggle! The lead character is Kantkiss Neverclean. She in involuntarily volunteered (SPOILER) by Slimey Sue into the Hunger Games for her sister. The Hunger Games is apparently the second highest rated television show after Extreme Home makeover in Peaceland. Kantkiss is apart of the District 12--- the Telemarketing District.  Here's what I felt about Allegiant about five months ago: 
 We can be mended. We mend each other. 
 How am I coping? Not well. 
 5 stars because it was amazing in all proportions. I try to find negative points but there's just none. 
 Before I start let me just point out some of my favorite quotes in Veronica Roth's finale, Allegiant: 
 1. "and I know the beauty he sees is just freedom -- freedom to be seen as a whole man instead of a damaged one." Tobias, 248 
 2. "It's strange, but there's something in that thought that makes me feel almost ...free." Tris, 187 
 3. "You don't believe things because they make your life better, you believe them because they're true." (I forgot, woops) 
 4. "It seems fitting that the blow would leave a mark on both on us. That's how the world works." Tris, 278. 
 5. "I choose him over and over again, and he chooses me." Tris, 372 
 6. "It's what you deserve to hear," I say firmly, my eyes going cloudy with tears. "That you're whole, that you're worth loving, that you're the best person I've ever known." Tris, 414 
 IF YOU DIDN'T READ DIVERGENT AND INSURGENT, THEN YOU REALLY SHOULD! 
 At this point, don't read this if you didn't read Allegiant! 
 In Allegiant, you will discover: 
 1. Lies, betrayal, and deceit. 
 2. The meaning behind Allegiant, as usual in all of the books. 
 3. How being Divergent just separates you from everyone else. 
 4. How being different from one another can lead to conflict. 
 5. The truth behind being a Dauntless... if you know what I mean. 
 6. Sacrifice to save one another. 
 7. and an unexpected ending. For me, I knew that either Tris or Tobias would pass, but I didn't expect it to be that drastic. 
 I feel like everything inside of me has been shattered because I haven't been attached to a book for so long. (The Fault in Our Stars is the first one.) There's just so much emotion in Allegiant that you're going to laugh, cry, fangirl, get mad, say no, say yes... 
 To further explain my feelings towards this book, I will do this through describing some characters in Allegiant. 
 Tris: She is the bravest character in Allegiant, hands down. I admire how deep her love and affection is towards her family and friends. I learned that to sacrifice is to show the greatest love for all. Yes, I was weeping when Veronica killed her off, but then if she lived, it wouldn't really feel realistic. Life is never easy. 
 Tobias: I started to hate him when he listened to Nita, instead of Tris. Because of the explosions my favorite character, Uriah, died. But then I admire him. He shows he's all strong and mighty, while in fact he is suffering in the inside. Reading his POV at the ending was very painful to bear. 
 Christina: Being Christina seriously sucks. Will and Uriah died and they were Christina's close friends. But then, just as what she said at the last page of the book, She's holding on to the moments that do not suck. The trick is to notice them when they come around. 
 Peter: Peter is one of my favorite characters ever since Divergent. I liked him because of his cruel and sinister personality, and after he swallowed the memory serum, I admired him even more because he realized that his doings were wrong, but then he can't do anything to change himself either. There are just some habits that will never go away, and when you're given the chance to take away with it by erasing memory, you have a choice to do so or not. I would take that choice, absolutely. 
 David: I think there was a point in his life where he could have just turned back time and maybe had a family with Natalie or something. Nothing hurts more than watching the one you love with another. But then love is also about making sure that person is at her happiest. Regarding about the experiments, it feels like that's the only thing keeping him going, now that Natalie is gone. And also that he is the head, he has the power. 
 Uriah: Okay, I should point out right now that Uriah and Peter are my favorite characters in the whole Divergent series. So when Zeke told Tobias to look after him, Veronica just gave me a dead giveaway that Uriah was going to die soon. Just when he was getting cozy with Christina... We didn't get to hear his famous last words! 
 Nita: I'm trying to figure out what to say about Nita... did her action proved her heroic or not? I don't know, maybe she was only thinking about the only option, but not the option that could save everyone, unlike Tris. I would love to learn more about her, actually. 
 All in all, the Divergent series was a success! I liked how in the end, there was no war because they were able to stop it before it happened. I liked how they tried to think of ways that would save more people instead of just one (as what Tris says.) It was only 2 chapters until the epilogue and I already missed reading from the mind of Tris. I'm pretty sure everyone misses her.

HHhH charms with its brilliance and capivates with its whim. The atrocities committed by Heydrich and those under his command are well known but surprisingly little is known about the brave men and women whose mission it was to end his reign of terror. 
 What is especially impressive about HHhH is how Binet tries to tell this remarkable story. All too often historical fiction and even historical work is tarnished by convenient untruths and grandiose embellishment. 
 Against this, HHhH is refreshing with its attempt to encourage the reader to reconstruct the truth surrounding the assassination attempt on Heydrich, even though our protagonist effectively deconstructs everything that he encounters in order to allow the reader to do so. Yet there are times where our protagonist cannot help himself and indulges in the dramatic flourish that he rails against. It is at these moments where the reader can appreciate the difficulty that storytellers face in capturing a true account of events 
 Personally I would be more inclined to dabble into historical fiction if its storytelling style continues along this new exciting path set down by Binet.

 Anyways, this book started off really strongly but I think it kind of lost some of its steam after the introduction, specifically when Door comes back for Richard and he officially joins their party to avenge her family . So, like, when the journey actually begins. The writing and humor was consistent throughout the whole book though, so that's good. I really liked the characters, and the premise of London Above and London Below is just so interesting. I also really liked the ending, I was scared for a moment that Gaiman would make it completely unsatisfying and have Richard be stuck in London Above, but alas, the Marquis came in clutch (as usual) and we once again get a happy ending :) . I would definitely be interesting in exploring this world some more, whether that be in another book or other media. 
 This is only my second Gaiman book, but I like it better than the first that I read from him (Stardust) and I'm very interesting in reading more. Perhaps I'll read his newest one next, or maybe American Gods, since that seems to be the most popular.

Well, where do I even start. 
 Let's start off with the fact that I came into this book completely blind; I had no idea what this book was about. In fact, for some reason I had this notion that this book was going to be about mental illness. 
 So, seeing as how I came into this book knowing nothing about it, imagine my surprise when I started reading it and I read nonsense. Turns out, this book is filled with a made up language based off of Russian slang. I saw some reviews praising the author for making the slang accessible and easy to follow and learn. All I have to say about that is 'speak for yourself.' I had no idea how to read this and I was barely getting along until I finally looked up a glossary and memorized a few of the more commonly used words. 
 Besides the difficulty I faced in reading this book, I guess I just don't "get it." The ultraviolence turned me off, which I guess was the point, however, I know a lot of people felt sorry for Alex and what he went through, well, not me. I'm not saying he deserved everything he got, but he deserved a lot of it. He was a borderline psychopath who got off on violence and being an overall shitty human being. I have no sympathy for what he went through. I think what made me lose any and all compassion I might have had for him is when he got two 10 year old girls drunk, brought them home, then raped them. 
 I don't get the theme warning about government control and whatever -- maybe they crossed the line but it's hard to care when the only example of that we're showed is what happened to Alex. 
 Overall, I thought this book sucked. I almost gave up after page 20 but I powered through thinking about all the good reviews on goodreads. In hindsight, I should have just read wikipedia. This book was a real pain in the ass to read. If anyone wants to try and explain to me whatever I'm not seeing, that'd be nice. Can't say I'd agree with you, though.

 3.5 stars. Okay. This book was a pretty solid 4 stars until the ending. I mean, if you read this book for what it is, you'll really enjoy it. What it is is a nice, easy, mindless, chick-lit book. It's a fast, easy read full of fluff and light teenage angst. So, I accepted that fact and I really enjoyed the book. The writing made me chuckle sometimes out loud but there were also times where I thought it was pretty cheesy (even for a chick-lit) and wondered if a guy really acted that way or would say that. Usually books with characters like these just annoy the crap out of me but somehow when Lauren Barnholdt writes them it's okay. Now, let's move on to the ending/my rant. Seriously, this book went from a solid 4 stars to 3/3.5 stars. I mean, I'd give the ending itself 2 stars. Obviously I said not to expect much from this book but I seriously expected more than what it is. Let me explain. Jace and Peyton hook up for one day but it's this crazy, out of this world, amazing day. Then they talk and whatnot. Then one day, Jace stops talking to her, and therefore, breaks up with her (even though they technically weren't even dating). And it's like Jace and Peyton still aren't over each other *cue eye roll* and somehow they end up on this sorta, kinda road trip together. Oh, and you find out they broke up because of this "secret" that Peyton kept from Jace...prepare for the ranting (It will most definitely contain spoilers so...) It turns out the "secret" that Peyton kept from Jace was that her parents were getting a divorce. What. The. Actual. Fuck. Okay, here's where I have a problem with this book. I was willing to overlook the fact that Peyton and Jace are unrealistically obsessed with each other after one day but I will not overlook this. Like, SERIOUSLY? THAT'S WHY HE WAS PISSED OFF AT HER? Are you fucking kidding me? Well, first off Jace, considering you guys only went on one date, it's no fucking wonder she didn't tell you that her parents were getting a divorce . She barely fucking knows you. She didn't even tell ANYONE yet, not even her best friend, or close family members, and you fucking expect her to tell you something that personal?! It obviously must devastate her. Why the fuck would you feel like she was obligated to tell you? It wasn't even a secret in a sense. It was her not ready to fucking share everything with you. That's so fucking stupid. If that was me I'd tell the guy to fuck off. Not like I owe it to him to tell him something that's personal and none of his business, especially if I've only known him for a few months. 
 Also, Peyton was just so stupid. Why the fuck she didn't tell her dad, or anyone, that her mom stole her identity is beyond me. Yeah, I get it. that sucks. It was out of nowhere and how the hell do you confront a parent? But seriously, your dad is a fucking option! HELLO?! I mean, yeah, take some time to digest it but completely doing nothing about it and "running away" is just ridiculous. How old is she again? 
 And Jordan giving that advice to Jace? Do teenage guys even think like that? And Jace and Peyton's povs sounded really similar. 
 There are plenty more things to complain about but I think it'll just take all day. I gave Two-Way Street (a similar book by the same author) 5 stars because I read it years ago when I was much younger and my tastes were not yet as mature and refined as they are now (pfft hahahahahaha. yeah right. like I can actually use the words mature and refined to describe myself. Probably more accurate to say I've slightly matured from pre-teen to young adult teen and therefore, now enjoy deeper reads.I still enjoy chick-lit every now and then though.), and the book was easy to read (I started and finished it on a Saturday morning) but I'm pretty sure if I re-read it now the rating would go down. Still, if you read the book for what it is and aren't expecting anything above superficiality then you'll be able to enjoy the book. 
 Plus there were a lot of things that didn't have closure. Also, why the heck even have B.J. in the book? And that scene with Jace's mom. Talk about cheesy and unrealistic. 
 Also the cameos with Courtney and Jordan seemed to be there just so they would have a cameo in the book. Lame.

*Sigh* Boy, was I disappointed from this book...I was expecting this book to be amazing because it has a pretty high rating (honestly, I should have learned my lesson from TFiOS) and that some reviewers that I follow have praised and lauded Ms. Stiefvater's other books. So, I obviously expected this book to be amazing. I was wrong. It was boring, lackluster, and plain. First off, the pacing. Literally nothing, NOTHING, happens in this book. Oh you can argue with that point but whatever. I first realized that nothing happened at around page 100 when Puck had FINALLY decided to register in the race on her regular horse. It's ridiculous that it took that long. Why? Because it's unnecessary and BECAUSE IT'S EXPLAINED IN THE SYNOPSIS. Ugh. Such a bad move. Then I read 300 more pages and I got near the end when finally, FINALLY, the race actually started. 
 ...Are you kidding me? The WHOLE book is superficial and composed of NOTHING. Seriously!! I get it, the men discriminate against you, Puck, because you're a girl. I understood that concept the first time it happened. No need to shove it in my face every chapter. You and Sean have this crazy love for horses that no one else apparently understands. Gotcha. Oh yeah, and it's a BIG deal because you're the first/only girl to decide to do this. Yeah, I GOT THE MEMO. The idea that a girl takes the first initiative to end something that has long time been a male dominated activity used to be original but now it's become cliche, expected even! The author literally could have written this book in like 100 pages or less. Seriously. (Also, the reason that Puck joined the races is incredibly stupid and shallow. Seriously? It's not believable enough for me.) 
 The author writes this book in alternating point of views. Puck and Sean. A.k.a. the female protagonist who is defying gender roles blah blah blah (not that that's not important but the way it was written was quite honestly, lame) and the male love interest (oh please, that's not even a spoiler. Seriously, did anyone NOT expect them to get together?) because you've got to add a little romance in here *sarcasm*. My main complaint with this style choice is that the tone of the povs ARE EXACTLY THE SAME. Sean and Puck sound exactly.the.same. I shit you not, I'm not even exaggerating or anything. I swear. Honest. I mean, if you're going to write multiple povs you HAVE to write them so they're different from one another (I think Rick Riordan is a GREAT example of this. His characters in the HoO series [while not all likable, at least to me] definitely all have unique voices. It's practically impossible to get them mixed up). Seriously, it's only two characters! You seriously couldn't create two different personalities? I mean, there's this one page where Sean remarks on how handsome this American guy is (another thing, the author created this world and decided to incorporate it somehow with reality. It's weird and awkward, at least for me). Do guys even do that?! 
 I did enjoy the ending but it definitely DOES NOT make up for reading a whole book worth of nothing. The ending, while pleasing, isn't even surprising either. It's expected. Not good. 
 This book unfortunately lacks originality. It falls into that young-adult-book category (I can't think of the word right now). Y'know, when all young adult books seem to follow this pattern? Boy-meets-girl or vice versa and they bond and they get together at the end and everything works out happily ever after after stumbling over a few conflicts here or there. I can't articulate myself right now but...yeah.

4.5 stars rounded up to 5. So I had high expectations coming into this book and the beginning was kind of slow but I'd say my expectations were surpassed.

It was a very clever addition that worked out because the other povs give us insight in how other people perceive August's facial deformities. It works so well because the author was spot on in her characterization of the characters. Their thoughts and their actions were 100% accurate/realistic and completely reflect how kids (and even adults) would act or think. Honestly, reading this transported me back to when I was in elementary school and I honestly emphasize so much. I was definitely one of those kids who didn't partake in bullying but I wouldn't stand up for the person either (I'm ashamed to say). 
 Kids and adults alike will enjoy this book and the message resonates no matter how old one may be. Everyone should be reminded of the message of this book and I genuinely think if I ever have a child/children I'm going to give them this book to read. I honestly teared up like twice throughout this book, but I'm a big sap, so.

 3.5 stars. At first, I couldn't get into this book, almost everyone is a shitty person. And I found it hard to believe that there was this extremely "popular" bitch girl who owned the school. And that there were teachers that shitty. This is what you see on tv or in books. It's not real life (hopefully). 
 However, I didn't want to stop reading. It's a very quick book to read and I finished it in a few hours, 3-4 at best. Some things don't get as resolved as you wished, Donnie almost raping Regina, Regina being a huge fucking bitch all those years and almost no repercussions . But the ending is still somewhat satisfying. 
 Regina was hard to sympathize with; you feel bad for her, or at least I did, but you also kind of hate her. In a sense, she became a victim of her own abuse. Or as the saying goes, "you reap what you sow." The book makes you think (when I say that I mean: it made me think), does Regina deserve what's happening to her? Does she deserve kindness? Personally, what does it say about me, that I enjoyed her petty revenges. That I was rooting for her to get back at Anna and Kara? That I was just as thrilled as she was at playing the same game as Anna and Kara, instead of being the bigger person? 
 That being said, I didn't get into this book at first but after a while, I couldn't stop reading it. 
 Also, what was up with the romance? How am I suppose to feel about that?
3.5 stars, was really liking this then the ending...Also, Grow some balls Dimmesdale, you're such a little bitch. Proudly shipping Dimmingworth <3

HOLY CRAP. MY FEELINGS.

Okay. First off, what I didn't like: 
 -the fact that this book felt way too much like a set up for The Dark Artifices 
 -not enough sizzy scenes 
 -way too many povs in the book. Half of them were just plain unnecessary and just muddled the story and dragged it on 
 -that the book is around 700 pages and there are times where it really feels like its lagging 
 -the fact that it feels like I'm missing out on so many references if I'm not caught up in all the shadowhunter facts and family tree and stuff 
 -how Cassandra Clare handled sizzy

 What I liked:

 My thoughts: 
 I feel like Helen and Aline were in the book for a reason. Like, there were a lot of scenes where they were mentioned, even if it was for a second or two. This makes me excited because they seem like a really interesting couple and I hope they play a role in TDA. Also, does anyone even really care about Maia or Jordan?

There were a lot of things in this book that I didn't expect. The direction it took, the mature content and themes ( The emphasis on the psychological and physical torture that was happening ), that one thing Adrian and Sydney get married! HOLY CRAP! (I literally yelled, "WHAT?" out loud when I read this part. I totally did NOT see it coming), I did, however, predict the ending even before reading the book. I predicted this from reading the synopsis for The Ruby Circle, so it's all good. The best book in the bloodlines series so far in my opinion. 
 This book isn't perfect, there were a lot of loose ends and questions that I hope aren't just left hanging and are answered in the last book, but it was pretty damn good.

Kind of sad this is the last book in the VA universe but alas, all good things must come to an end. I really enjoyed this ride. Also, what is it with authors always bringing back a villain that's supposed to have died or be done with? I mean, it happened in the TMI and a bunch of other works. Just curious.

Oh my. I can't even. Ugh. I knew I should have waited until the next book came out before I read this one. I can't even process anything. Sydney, girl, I'm here for you. Probably my favorite book from this series so far...Also, the cameos = amazing. I seriously feel like re-reading the Vampire Academy series again...maybe I will around the time the movie comes out. 
 It has a cover! At first, I thought it was just so...awkward. It still kind of is but it's grown on me. Sydney looks kind of flushed and disheveled which shows just how much she's grown!

Dat ending doe. Starting from Sydney's revelation to the very end, it was amazing. Faith in this series has been restored after a very disappointed The Golden Lily book. Cannot wait for The Fiery Heart! Also, I kind of missed seeing Jill in this book. I know she had her moments but not nearly enough imo. And having that little snippet with Rose makes me so nostalgic!

So many mixed emotions about this book. 4.5 stars. I honestly liked the writing and I thought the book was pretty realistic. What killed it was the ending. Not so much that it was supposedly a cliffhanger (because to me, it honestly wasn't) but just the ending itself. It's like this beautiful story with this horrible ending. I can't really imagine what would happen after he started running. What would happen to the family, and Cami? I can't imagine how the mom must be feeling. I felt as though the ending killed me just as it did the mom. The ending was very abrupt. It felt like this amazing story and the author just didn't quite knew how to finish it so she cut it off with this crazy ending that just didn't seem to fit in with the book. Kind of like Lois Duncan's books (huge fan of her books by the way). Like, the ending snaps you out of the feeling you get when you get absorbed into a book, and back into reality.

*Post-reading*. Welcome back Sarah Dessen. This book was amazing! For some reason I felt incredibly attached to Emaline and her problems/pain were my problems/pain, at least while reading. This was an incredible book as compared to her previous one What Happened to Goodbye. I should probably re-read it but I don't recall it being as engaging. Anyways, maybe it's the fact that I'm older but I really loved how this book seems like it's just a romance book but it's really not. In fact, the romance takes a back seat. Anyways, excited for what other book she writes up next! 
 New Sarah Dessen novel! YES *fistpump*! But wait, what is this? The author's name is bigger than the book's title! .... *facepalm*. Seriously though, am I the only one who hates that? Anyways, super excited for this new novel!
There's just something that prevents the books in this series from getting 5 stars...

The book that got me into PJ. This was my first Percy Jackson book that I read. I remember being at the library and wanting to find a book to read and seeing this book and remembering reading about how Percy Jackson was being made into a movie or something and deciding to read this book because of that. One of the best decisions I have ever made in my life. It introduced me to my favorite book series. Literally the next day, I was at a bookstore and I had my dad spend $100 on the box set without even knowing what the books were about (other than they were Percy Jackson) and having no idea whatsoever if I would even like it.

I liked it. I especially liked the beginning, the sarcastic, humorous tone of the book, and the action. It got kind of slow in the beginning/middle and the romance was sweet but kind of sickly because, you know, it was basically necrophilia . What I didn't like was how the beginning high school stuff was cliche, the assumption that all a guy has to do is ignore a girl to get her to fall for you, and the idea of a stereotypical white, blonde prom queen (although I actually liked the character). Also I don't know how to feel about the ending. But, there's a sequel so.

Was disappointed in this book. Like many others have already said, the way Maas describes Celeana it seems like she's ass kicking, kinda-cold heartedish BAMF. But the Celeana we read isn't that, sure she has her moments but for the most part it's HUGE telling-not-showing. For the full experience I HIGHLY suggest reading the novellas first! You won't regret it :D (seriously I enjoyed the novellas more than this book). still, looking forward to the next one. Also let it be known that I read this book around right when it came out and I PREDICT CHAOL WILL END UP WITH CELAENA IN THE END. That's right, I can already tell Chaol will end up with her, and I will feel shamelessly vindicated when this happens in the end. But I'm Team Dorian anyways :p

4.5 stars...or 5? This book was REALLY uncomfortable for me to read (mostly the beginning) . Especially since this book portrays the abuser as someone who is so different than how it is normally portrayed. For example, in most books, if the main character (usually a girl, haven't read one about a boy yet but who knows)is sexually abused, it is usually by maybe a close male figure. Nope, not in this book (kinda). So, kudos to the author. Leah was a mystery for me. I felt like I knew her personality and why she does what she does but then she does something or says something and I'm back to square one. I'm just as lost as Laine as to Leah's personality. I knew or I FELT really that she was being abused by Sam because of the seemingly obvious hints but then later I would be so unsure of myself. Like what I thought the reason for something happening wasn't actually the reason at all. Really, I felt like Laine, I felt like Leah was manipulating me (so, that's amazing. I mean, for a book to make me feel like the protagonist does? For me to have my feelings and thoughts manipulated? It doesn't sound like a good thing but I don't think a book has ever made me feel that way as strongly as this book does). In the beginning I was annoyed at Laine for being so weak. I thought Leah was just a manipulative b**ch oh sure, she's a victim yes but in the end she was still a manipulative b**ch. Yes, she was probably that way because of the things she experience but still...Somehow by the middle of the book I was SYMPATHIZING with her. I felt sorry for her, even though I still looked down at her for how she treated Laine. It's complicated.

Unsure whether or not to rate this 4 or 5 stars. For sure though, this book is not for everyone. Especially if you disagree with the main character's views (political, religious etc). Personally there were times I couldn't stand Cole and was in disbelief as to why Ashley just accepted what happened. If there's one thing to learn from this book is that love demands sacrifice and compromise.

The end. Don't mean to sell this book short but it's nothing new to me.

Team Jem...or I will burn the book and throw it against the wall.

Anyways, let's talk about other relationships. Gabriel and Cecily anyone? OMG They are ADORABLE. Favorite couple besides Jem and Tessa. Also, I actually didn't mind Will in this book. I KNEW she was going to end up with Will (she technically did, and it says on the family tree too) but I didn't expect her to also end up with Jem...it's too good to be true. Seriously, this was too much for my feels to handle.

OH MY GOSH. I just finished the book and am still reeling from it. 3.5-4ish stars. I loved the lore in this book. The reason this book isn't rated higher is because it took forever to get interesting. I literally could not get into it until around page 300 where Madrigal and the wishbone situation was finally introduced. . Seriously, I didn't care about Karou at all and it was only slightly interesting when she and Akiva finally met. But man, oh man. When the story becomes about Madrigal ... Wow. I definitely would have liked this book more if there were less Karou and more Madrigal . More M and less Karou would have been amazing. This book was like it rollercoaster: it takes FOREVER to get to the climax, but when it does...it doesn't stop or slow down and you want MORE. The romance is definitely the best aspect of this book. Which is disappointing b/c the author tries to bring other sub-plots to support the main romance one but they're extremely weak.
Favorite book in the series.

The first time I read this I rated it 4 stars because before I read it my friends told me that people thought it wasn't as good as the previous books. Stupidly, I let others' opinions influence me before I even read it. I reread it a second time and it is fucking brilliant .
Hey! No pointless love triangle? YES PLEASE! :D

4.5 stars. 
 A very strong debut novel. The premise was interesting and I was looking forward to reading this book. I can't believe it took me 5 years since first adding this to my to-read list to finally read it. But, I have, so yay for me. 
 I really like June and I think she's kick ass. Day's pretty awesome too but I enjoyed June's povs more. I'm also iffy about the romance -- it just didn't seem that organic/believable to me. Let's be real, it totally wasn't, but I'm not saying I want slow burn, I just want something that cultivates after a little more time and experience spent together and a little more getting to know you, instead of the "instant-attraction-I-don't-know-why-but-I'm-just-drawn-to-you" type thing. Thankfully the romance wasn't that big of a thing so it wasn't too bad. 
 The beginning started off kind of slow (in my opinion) but, as everyone else says, the rest of the book is pretty fast paced and I didn't want to put it down. I agree with someone calling this book a little too formulaic, which is pretty true since that's what I thought when I finished the book. It follows the very tried and true (but still awesome) format of YA dystopian fiction. I'm a little disappointed the book ended where it did -- I was kind of hoping more would happen but I know the author's saving that for the rest of the trilogy. 
 I hope the 2nd and 3rd book are just as good as this book because honestly, YA dystopian trilogies have a tendency to have a kick ass first novel but then once the dystopian world has been established the 2nd and 3rd novel usually tend to take a completely different direction and end up being disappointing (*cough* looking at you Divergent trilogy *cough*). 
 I'm excited to read the next two books. Here's to hoping they're just as good. 
 P.S. Yay for Asian representation! Universe knows we need more of it!
Couldn't finish it. I was 5/6 of the way done with the book and I just had to put it down because it was so boring. Nothing exciting happened and I felt like the book was dragging.

Probably 90% of the characters annoyed the crap out of me and I had to make myself suffer through the book because I have to finish reading a book I start. Overall, it was okay, it wasn't mind-blowing or incredibly amazing but it was a nice read. The plot wasn't original but the author somehow made it seem less cliche that it really was. The ending is pretty open-ended though, the only thing that was set in stone was Anna and St. Clair ending up together, which, come on, you have to be a thick-headed person to not think that they would end up together from since the beginning of the book. We don't know what happened to Amanda and Dave and Bridgette (which I really wanted to know because although she wasn't a major character, she didn't really annoy me as much and I liked her) and all that good stuff . The author's writing was confusing at some parts i.e. time passes by (like say, a day) and we are unaware of it and are completely caught off guard when the next chapter just abruptly switches to a different location and topic, ect.
Wow...Read it.

2.5 stars. Was this book mind-blowing? No. Did it change my life? No. Was it funny and quirky? Not particularly. Did I enjoy it nonetheless? Yes. It's a book that offers insight into the world of mental illness, and considering I'm majoring in psychology, fits. I do have to say though, that the synopsis made the book sound more interesting than it is.

I LOVED Hate List by Jennifer Brown so when I found out that she wrote a second novel I knew I just HAD to read it. Boy, was I disappointed. The book starts off interesting enough but once Cole, Alex's new found boyfriend, starts showing signs of abuse and possessiveness the book just goes downhill. Alex's best friends are love-able but once she starts dating Cole you just want to strangle them! The book was pretty slow and didn't have much going for it, besides the abusive boyfriend plot, nothing interesting really happened. I'd recommend this book for anyone who is interested in a young adult book about abusive relationships but only if you have nothing better to read. There are SO many other abusive relationship books that are 10x better. Honestly, I kind of wished that I hadn't read this because it was just such a step back from Hate List. All I can do is eagerly await Jennifer Brown's next novel and hope that it leans more towards a Hate List kind of book.

I was gonna give this book 3 stars, but I decided on 2 because justifying attempted rape is never o.k. 
 I felt like this book set out to be one of those deep, pretentious books that set out to give you life lessons. I will admit that it did a good job of not being pretentious. It was extremely emotionally manipulative, however.
Ahh read this in middle school, I think either 6th or 7th grade. It was my first verse book and I fell in love...

Let me just say that before I read this book I liked to think of myself and neutral and leaning toward Team Unicorn...Now, post-reading of this book, it is safe to say that I am Team Zombie. The zombie stories were brilliant and excellent, the unicorn stories (with the exception of 2-3 stories) were just plain horrible and stupid.

How do I even begin to describe this book? I love it so much. I love Markus Zusak's writing style. This book, if I had to describe it in one word, is charming. The writing is charming, the characters are charming, the story is charming. The book is charming. This book is the kind that you just can't rush through. I admit, sometimes I start skimming through books. I tried to do it with this book. Big mistake. First, what was I thinking trying to skim parts of this? No. This book requires you to take your time and read it at the book's pace. You can't rush it. You have to read each and every word because every single word is important. But you will enjoy it immensely. The characters truly shine in this story. No matter how unlikable they are (or seem to be). I loved every. single. one. My favorites just might be Rudy and Ilsa(a.k.a the mayor's wife). Near the end of the book I started bawling. I was crying so hard. And I loved it. I loved that this book evoked that emotion out of me. In fact, I was so overwhelmed that I just had to put the book down and cry. I had to stop reading, put my head down, and just cry. I would then compose myself and start again - only to read the next sentence or two and just burst out in tears again. Part of it because the sentence made me cry. And part of it because I was still overwhelmed and the sentence pushed me over the edge (so to speak) again. This is a book that will make me reel. I'll need days to recover from this book.

Wow. What a ride. 
 I'm so pleasantly impressed by this book. I came in expecting this to be another YA dystopian novel -- and it is -- but it's so much more. In fact, it reads more like a fantasy novel, including the large world building and huge adventure the protagonist goes on. 
 I didn't like the beginning of the book, the writing took a while to get used to and it was just really slow in the beginning. I also felt like Patrick Ness dragged out the "secret" of how boys turn into men a little too long. Also, the whole "if we can turn you into a killer Todd Hewitt, that proves we'll be able to turn anyone!" thing was so stupid. There's just not a lot of sense and rationality in that line of thinking, which may be the point but to make that the driving plot point, well, it just doesn't really work. 
 I was surprised to see the length of the book, but like I said, it's almost a fantasy book. In fact, this book really reminds me of the video game "Fallout 3." All I could think about was Todd being the main character in this post-apocalyptic world filled with moral ambiguity and a shit ton of guns and killing. It's pretty great and very fitting. 
 It took a while to warm up to this book but I'm very eager to start reading the second book! 
 (Also, they're making a movie with Tom Holland, Daisy Ridley, and a bunch of other well known celebrity actors. I'm impressed with the cast.)

I feel like I would have appreciated this book even more if I read "A Wrinkle in Time" beforehand. 
 Anyways, I wasn't really feeling the time travel stuff but everything else, the friendship/family dynamics were A+.

I need time to process this... 4.5 stars 
 Okay. I LOVED this book. Daniel Handler's writing is unique and it's great! The characters were (mostly) likable and the whole story/romance didn't come off as unrealistic to me. Of course we all know that Ed and Min broke up and the reason why isn't exactly original or jaw-dropping but when we find out Ed cheated on Min well, damn. I felt just as equally heart broken and betrayed as Min did. And if I read a book and it can evoke real emotions out of me like that, or make me feel like the protagonist does well, then I have complete and utter respect for the author. I immensely wanted to buy this book while I was reading it (honestly I developed a little sweet crush on Ed myself) but when I finished I didn't have the feeling of wanting to re-read it anymore; because I felt betrayed by Ed . Still, I think I'll pick this book up next time I'm at the book store :) (Also some sentences were kind of confusing but it makes sense I suppose, since this whole book is a letter written from Min, who is just a high school student and therefore, perfection cannot be expected.) See I'm pretty sure that sentence I just wrote is wrong.

I would probably rate this book 3 stars. Okay, so let's start this review; first off, I loved how the author was able to have several different sub-plots going on at once with all the different characters and not have it all end up in confusion. She pulled it off, which is probably a hard thing to do, but she did it. That's not to say that I didn't have any issues with this book, because there were a lot. First off, it was pretty inconsistent now that I think about it. It's just the little things, like for example Simon and Isabelle's relationship. Honestly, I thought they were already dating by the time this book started but no, they were still in the confusion zone of almost boyfriend and girlfriend, but not quite there yet. Really? Like, even at the end of the book, after all the intimate moments they shared, they're STILL not dating? And neither of them is apparently bright enough to figure out that they both love each other? Did the stuff that happened in the previous books not matter either? That's not to say that their relationship was probably the saving grace of this book for me... . 
 Also, the author uses the same adjectives/phrases for probably every character. Honestly, how many times do you need to tell us Jace is golden, or Sebastian has Valentine's hair and it suits him better than when he dyed it black? 
 And Clary and Jace. Just,...really? REALLY? They were beyond annoying for most of this book, although there WERE some moments in which they were tolerable. Clary was SO selfish and their romance just resembles Edward's and Bella's from Twilight so much. 
 Jace: I hurt you, I can't be with you anymore now, even though I love 
 you and want to be with you! It's all my fault that you got hurt! (Mind you that I had this annoyance since the start of the series, surprisingly Jace wasn't the culprit in this book though!) 
 Clary: I don't care if you want to die! I love you too much and i'm so selfish that i'm going to make everything worse! I'm going to ignore what everyone tells me to do because I can't lose you; I love you so much that I can't live without you! (Really Clary? *sarcasm* How did you possibly survive before Jace came into your life? Clary was fine throughout the series but recently she's starting to annoy the crap out of me.) 
 I have mixed feelings about how the author wrote about one couple or some group of characters and their adventure and then end the chapter on a cliffhanger. And then the next chapter...SURPRISE! starts right off with a different group of characters...like how she wrote about Simon and Isabelle and then suddenly alternates back to Jace and Clary...Although, at first I was incredibly annoyed, eventually I would warm up and start to get sucked into an adventure only to have the whole process repeat itself. 
 But honestly, Isabelle and Simon...DAWWWW THEY'RE SO CUTE! Favorite couple (are they even an official couple?) from the series!

I was debating on whether or not to give this book 2 or 3 starts. I decided 3 because I just loved Vampire Academy and Richelle Mead but this book certainly is NOWHERE NEAR her best. First, the book was SO predictable. I knew from Bloodlines that Adrian and Sydney would be the book's main couple just like Rose and Dimitri from VA. *facepalm* Sydney is supposedly smart so you know that she would catch on pretty quickly to what was going to happen/what was happening right? Nope. She is like a slug in figuring things out, SLOW. About 1/6 through the book I had already guessed on what was going to happen and I was correct. The book honestly didn't have much going for it, incredibly predictable from close to the beginning all the way to the ending. On the bright side, I just LOVED Adrian's love confession, even though it was borderline cliche, I believe he somewhat pulled it off :).

So I really enjoyed like the first 3/4 of the book and I definitely would have gave it a solid 4 stars until I got near the ending and John Green started writing his stupid, annoying metaphors. That itself is enough to merit a full drop of one star, from a 4 star book to a 3 star book. The ending just kind of sucked. The last paragraph itself is fine and kind of cute but the ending is where John Green just starts taking over and instead of the characters talking, it's just John Green talking to the reader to get across a philosophical, pretentious life theme. Seriously, like once Margo started spewing out stuff about paper towns and paper girls at the end I was gone and I didn't want to come back. I felt like Margo's characterization was choppy, and one could argue that's cause we see her from Q's point of view, but I blame it on poor execution. Basically, I enjoyed the first half of the story, it kind of dragged in the middle, and the ending sucked.

...disappointed at all the hype this book had but I guess it just wasn't the book for me. If I had to describe it in one word, PRETENTIOUS. Also, it didn't help that halfway through the book I was extremely bored and I had to FORCE myself to finish it...maybe I'm missing something?

It was an easy, quick read. Heard some good things about it so I'd thought I'd check it out. Was pretty disappointed after I read the book. It isn't all that great and there were many times where I just wanted to strangle the main character for being so slow and dumb and unable to comprehend the events that were clearly happening right in front of her. I didn't understand where the book was going with the romance, one moment one guy would be just friends with her and then all of sudden, he suddenly decides that he is in love with her. Overall, just like my rating shows, the book was o.k.
R.I.P. Ms. Harper Lee, Feb. 19, 2016. Thank you for writing one of the great American novels.

The synopsis of this book caught my attention right away. It intrigued me and after I read the back cover of this book on Amazon I immediately ordered it and was excited for it to come. I had no knowledge of the author or book other than what I read on the back. This is Jennifer Brown's debut novel but it doesn't seem like it.
